Built for everyone. Marlowby aims to meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA, the standard behind the ADA guidance for websites. Here is what that means on this site and how we checked it.

Text meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast. Every color pair was measured, including text over the hero sky, where a scrim keeps the headline readable as clouds drift behind it. Pages reflow at 400% zoom without sideways scrolling.
Every link, button, map pin and form control works from the keyboard, with a visible focus ring. A skip link jumps past the menu. Buttons and links are at least 44 by 44 pixels for touch.

Headings follow in order on every page. Images have text alternatives, and the 3D scenes, which are decorative, are hidden from screen readers with a written description in their place. Search results, FAQ filters, votes and form errors are announced as they change.
If your device asks for reduced motion, the scroll effects, the rotating city name and the box animations stay still. The scrolling announcement bar has a pause button.
Every field has a visible label. Errors appear next to the field and are linked to it, and checkout states every charge and renewal before you agree to it.
Box photos are ordinary image files, so they appear without WebGL. The site is tested in Chrome and in Safari’s WebKit engine, and keeps working offline after your first visit.

Every page passes the W3C HTML validator with no errors and scores 100 for accessibility in Google Lighthouse. We tested keyboard use by hand, measured contrast for each color pair, and checked the site in Chrome and Safari’s WebKit engine, with motion on and off.
